## Set Up Environment
```{r setup, include=FALSE}

library(mpmi)
library(ggplot2)
library(ks)
library(mvtnorm)
library(dplyr)
library(readxl)

```

## AIM

Our goal here is to use the Mutual Information metric to quantify the extent 
to which the spatial coordinates and projection-group (ORB, RSC, ORB-RSC) of
EC L5a neurons co-vary.

## Get Data

```{r get_data}

path = getwd()
data = read_csv(paste0(path,"/preprocessed_data/master_detailed_comment.csv"))
data$proj[data$neuron_ID == "1114_10"] <- "rsp_orb"
data$proj[data$neuron_ID == "1849931_7"] <- "rsp_orb"

# filter for rows with projection values

data = data[data$proj %in% c("rsp", "orb", "rsp_orb"),]

# remove all neurons from brain 1849929
data = data %>% filter(mouseID != 1849929)

print(head(data))
```

Here we extract our "projection" and "coordinate" info as two separate matrices.

```{r format_coords}

coords = as.matrix(select(data, x, y, z))

proj = as.matrix(data$proj)

```


Sara Wade has created a function, based on the mpmi package, which lets us 
calculate the Mutual Information between a continuous and a categorical value.

Our continuous variable is multi-dimensional, so native mpmi functionality only
reports the pairwise mutual info metrics (e.g. x_proj, y_proj, z_proj).

This function, however, returns a single mutual information metric:
xyz_proj. 

A fuller exploration of Sara's Code is available in mi.R

## Original MI Function

```{r mi_function}

mi = function(x,y, S= 5000, compute.entropy = TRUE){
  
  n = length(y)
  p = dim(x)

  # Step 1: compute kde for the coordinates
  kde.x = kde(x, supp = 10)

  # Step 2: compute kde for each group
  cats = unique(y)
  kde.groups = lapply(cats, function(c){ kde(x[y==c,], supp = 10)})

  # Draw importance samples from proposal
  y.is = matrix(sample(cats,S, replace = TRUE, prob = table(y)/n), S, 1)
  x.is = t(apply(y.is, 1, function(c){
     i = sample(which(y==c), size =1)
     rmvnorm(1, mean = x[i,], sigma = kde.groups[[which(c==cats)]]$H)
  }))

  # Calculate IS estimate of MI
  mi.is =  sapply(1:S,function(s){
    log2(predict(kde.groups[[which(y.is[s]==cats)]], x = x.is[s,] ))  -  log2(predict(kde.x, x = x.is[s,]))
  })

  e.x = NA
  if(compute.entropy==TRUE){
    # Compute entropy of x
    x.is.all = t(sapply(1:S, function(s){
      i = sample(1:n, size =1)
      rmvnorm(1, mean = x[i,], sigma = kde.x$H)
    }))
    e.s = sapply(1:S,function(s){
      -log2(predict(kde.x, x = x.is.all[s,]))
    })
    e.x = mean(e.s)
  }
  
  e.y = NA
  if(compute.entropy==TRUE){
    # Compute entropy of y
    py = table(y)/n
    e.y = sum(-py*log2(py))
  }

  return(list(mi = mean(mi.is), kde.x = kde.x, kde.groups = kde.groups, entrop.x = e.x, entrop.y = e.y))
}


```

## Calculate the "observed" Mutual Information

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}

x1 = coords
y1 = proj

mi.xy = mi(x1, y1)

print(paste("MI:", round(mi.xy$mi,3)))

# normalize to unit interval
norm_mi = round(mi.xy$mi/max(dmi(cbind(y1,y1))$mi[1,1],mi.xy$entrop.x),3)

# Normalize to the unit interval by dividing by the max entropies
print(paste("Normalized MI:", norm_mi))

```

Normalized MI = 0.043

Value is above zero - but is it significantly above zero?
To do this, we can check if the 95% Confidence Interval of the Sampling 
Distribution contains zero.

And we can generate this Sampling Distribution via Bootstrapping.

## Normalization Update (from Sara Wade)

Various different proposals exist to normalize the MI. 
One option is to divide by the maximum of the entropies.

Another is the Uncertainty Coefficient, which divides by the entropy of 𝑦
; Given the coordinates, how well can we determine the projection type?

The MI function has been updated to return the enthropy of y: here we use that
value to calculate the Uncertainty Coefficient.

```{r}

uncer_coeff = mi.xy$mi/mi.xy$entrop.y

# Normalize to the unit interval by dividing by the max entropies
print(paste("Uncertainty Coefficient:", round(uncer_coeff, 3)))

```

Uncertainty Coefficient: 0.833

## Bayesian Bootstrapping

Using the above function worked for the empirical data, but resulted in the 
return of Inf/-Inf/NaN values during bootstrapping. This was due to resampling
sometimes created bootstrapped datasets with very low variability / too many 
duplicate values. 

We get around this problem by using Bayesian Bootstrapping, via an updated MI
function.

https://matteocourthoud.github.io/post/bayes_boot/
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/r-language/dirichlet-distribution-in-r/

```{r bayes_boot_mi}

mi_bayes = function(x,y, S= 5000, compute.entropy = TRUE){
  
  n = length(y)
  p = dim(x)
  
  # generate weights using the dirichlet Distribution
  weights = n * as.numeric(gtools::rdirichlet(1, rep(1, n)))

  # Step 1: compute kde for the coordinates
  kde.x = kde(x, supp = 10, w = weights)

  # Step 2: compute kde for each group
  cats = unique(y)
  kde.groups = lapply(cats, function(c){ kde(x[y==c,], supp = 10,
                                             w = weights[y==c])})

  # Draw importance samples from proposal
  py_weighted = sapply(cats, function(c){sum(weights[y==c])/n})
  y.is = matrix(sample(cats,S, replace = TRUE, prob = py_weighted), S, 1)
  x.is = t(apply(y.is, 1, function(c){
     i = sample(which(y==c), size =1, prob = weights[y==c]/sum(weights[y==c]))
     rmvnorm(1, mean = x[i,], sigma = kde.groups[[which(c==cats)]]$H)
  }))

  # Calculate IS estimate of MI
  mi.is =  sapply(1:S,function(s){
    log2(predict(kde.groups[[which(y.is[s]==cats)]], x = x.is[s,] ))  -  log2(predict(kde.x, x = x.is[s,]))
  })

  e.x = NA
  if(compute.entropy==TRUE){
    # Compute entropy of x
    x.is.all = t(sapply(1:S, function(s){
      i = sample(1:n, size =1, prob = weights/sum(weights))
      rmvnorm(1, mean = x[i,], sigma = kde.x$H)
    }))
    e.s = sapply(1:S,function(s){
      -log2(predict(kde.x, x = x.is.all[s,]))
    })
    e.x = mean(e.s)
  }
  
  e.y = NA
  if(compute.entropy==TRUE){
    # Compute entropy of y
    e.y = sum(-py_weighted*log2(py_weighted))
  }

  return(list(mi = mean(mi.is), kde.x = kde.x, kde.groups = kde.groups, entrop.x = e.x, entrop.y = e.y))
}

```



No more pre-function re-sampling should be needed. These two calls should return
different MI values, even though they accept the same input data.

```{r test_m_weights}

# test 1
mi.t1 = mi_bayes(x1, y1)
print(paste("MI:", round(mi.t1$mi,3)))

# Normalize to the unit interval by dividing by the max entropies
norm1_mi_t1 = mi.t1$mi/max(mi.t1$entrop.y, mi.t1$entrop.x)
print(paste("Normalized MI (by max):", round(norm1_mi_t1,3)))

# Normalize to the unit interval by dividing by the entropy of y
norm2_mi_t1 = mi.t1$mi/mi.t1$entrop.y
print(paste("Uncertainty Coefficient:", round(norm2_mi_t1,3)))

```


```{r}

# test 2
mi.t2 = mi(x1, y1)
print(paste("MI:", round(mi.t2$mi,3)))

# normalize to unit interval
norm1_mi_t2 = mi.t2$mi/max(mi.t2$entrop.y, mi.t2$entrop.x)
norm2_mi_t2 = mi.t2$mi/mi.t2$entrop.y
# Normalize to the unit interval by dividing by the max entropies
print(paste("Normalized MI (by max):", round(norm1_mi_t2,3)))

# Normalize to the unit interval by dividing by the entropy of y
print(paste("Uncertainty Coefficient:", round(norm2_mi_t2,3)))


```

## Bootstrapping (Sara)

```{r}

B =1000 # Number of bootstrap repetitions

bootstrap_nMIs = sapply(1:B, function(b){
  # separate re-sampled X and Y matrices
  x_r = as.matrix(select(data, x, y, z))
  y_r = as.matrix(data$proj)
  
  # calculate new MI
  mi.r = mi_bayes(x_r, y_r)
  
  # get normalized mi
  norm1_mi = mi.r$mi/max(mi.r$entrop.y,mi.r$entrop.x)
  norm2_mi = mi.r$mi/mi.r$entrop.y
  return(c(norm1_mi, norm2_mi))
})

```

# Visualize Bootstrap Sampling Distribution (post-Sara Block)

```{r}

# remove any inf and na values from the vector
bootstrap_nMI1s = bootstrap_nMIs[1,]
bootstrap_nMI2s = bootstrap_nMIs[2,]
bootstrap_nMI1s = bootstrap_nMI1s[!is.na(bootstrap_nMI1s) & !is.infinite(bootstrap_nMI1s)]
bootstrap_nMI2s = bootstrap_nMI2s[!is.na(bootstrap_nMI2s) & !is.infinite(bootstrap_nMI2s)]


```

```{r bs_norm_mi}

# Plot histogram with quantiles
qs = quantile(bootstrap_nMI1s, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x=bootstrap_nMI1s), fill = "lightgray") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = qs[1], color = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = qs[2], color = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(bootstrap_nMI1s), color = "black") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x="normalized mutual information")


```

```{r}

print(paste0('Normalized MI (by max): ', mean(bootstrap_nMI1s),' [', qs[1], ', ', qs[2],']'))

```

```{r bs_uncer_coeff}

# Plot histogram with quantiles
qs = quantile(bootstrap_nMI2s, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

  geom_vline(xintercept = qs[2], color = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(bootstrap_nMI2s), color = "black") +

```

## Stat Tests

```{r}

pnorm(norm1_mi, mean = 0, sd = sd(bootstrap_nMI1s), lower.tail = FALSE)

```


```{r}

pnorm(norm2_mi, mean = 0, sd = sd(bootstrap_nMI2s), lower.tail = FALSE)

```

```{r}

# If the uncertainty coefficient is truly 1, what is the probability of observing
# a UC as small as the observed UC or smaller?
pnorm(norm2_mi, mean = 1, sd = sd(bootstrap_nMI2s), lower.tail = TRUE)

```

## One-Tailed T-test Alternative

```{r}

t_stat = (norm1_mi - 0) / sd(bootstrap_nMI1s)


pt(t_stat, df = (length(bootstrap_nMI1s) - 1), lower.tail = FALSE)

```

```{r}

t_stat = (norm2_mi - 0) / sd(bootstrap_nMI2s)


pt(t_stat, df = (length(bootstrap_nMI2s) - 1), lower.tail = FALSE)

```

```{r}

t_stat = (norm2_mi - 1) / sd(bootstrap_nMI2s)


pt(t_stat, df = (length(bootstrap_nMI2s) - 1), lower.tail = TRUE)

```

## Permutation Test Alternative

```{r}

P =1000 # Number of permutations

permuted_nMIs = sapply(1:P, function(p){
  # separate re-sampled X and Y matrices
  x_r = as.matrix(select(data, x, y, z))
  y_r = as.matrix(data$proj)
  n = length(y_r)
  perm = sample(c(1:n), size = n, replace=FALSE)
  x_r = x_r[perm,]
  
  # calculate new MI
  mi.r = mi(x_r, y_r)
  
  # get normalized mi
  norm1_mi = mi.r$mi/max(mi.r$entrop.y,mi.r$entrop.x)
  norm2_mi = mi.r$mi/mi.r$entrop.y
  return(c(norm1_mi, norm2_mi))
})

```

```{r}

print(paste('Permutation test p-value:',mean(permuted_nMIs[1,]>norm1_mi)))

```

```{r}

print(paste('Permutation test p-value:',mean(permuted_nMIs[2,]>norm2_mi)))

```
